note: Canonical permission lists for the LEAD runtime, installed by ops/bootstrap/install-harness.mjs into ~/.claude/settings.json. Edit here, re-run the installer; edits to the installed copy are overwritten, exactly like the instruction block. `platforms` narrows an entry to the platforms where it means anything — a PowerShell rule on a Mac is noise that hides the real list, and a Git-Bash home path does not exist there. `machine` is a value computed on the target machine at install time, the same scheme as `{repo}` in codex-trust.json: `ssh-host` installs the rule only when this HOME's ~/.ssh/config defines that Host alias. platforms answers which OS, not whose machine — an ssh alias, a checkout path or a disk name is a machine value and must not appear as a bare rule. An entry with neither applies everywhere. The deny list carries no Bash rule on purpose: the desktop app shows its terminal approval card while any shell rule sits in deny or ask, so recursive forced deletion is refused by the PreToolUse hook ops/bootstrap/shell-delete-hook.mjs instead (decisions #14075/#14077).
